tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run a Node command. Give its purpose and call directly for approval. Prefer file, search and edit tools for supported work. Bundled skill paths outside the workspace require unrestricted access. Foreground commands stop on exit, cancellation or timeout. Use background=true (not shell &) for servers, watchers, REPLs and other open-ended commands. It returns an ID immediately, has no timeout and records completion. Give event waits their own timeout. Check readiness with read_command, the ID, wait_ms and readiness text in until. Avoid sleep or curl loops. Background stdin works with or without a PTY. write_command queues input. Read output to confirm acceptance. Output reports truncation. Use stop_command to stop a process. Stopping the turn stops non-service commands and defers completion reports until the user's next message.

access.description: Sandboxed workspace commands on macOS/Linux need no approval. Writes stay in the worktree or temp directory. Network is blocked. Existing Git metadata and managed child worktrees are protected. macOS also blocks new .git paths. Request unrestricted for Git writes (including git init, add and commit), network or outside paths. Ask and Project require fresh approval per unrestricted command. With sandbox off, on Windows or in Full mode, every command runs unrestricted under the current permission mode.

cwd.description: Defaults to the admitted worktree. Relative paths resolve there. Workspace access confines cwd to it.

follow_up.description: Set when waiting for or monitoring a background command to resume on completion. Otherwise only the result is retained. A 15-minute silence triggers one stall notice and execution continues. Foreground commands backgrounded by user guidance get the same notice.

service.description: Requires background=true. Only for servers or watchers the user keeps running after the turn. Never use for builds or tests.

attachments.description: IDs copied to SAILRY_ATTACHMENTS/<id> for this command only. Use the shell's variable and path syntax. Edits affect only the copies.

pty.description: Requires background=true. Use for terminal prompts, REPLs or debuggers. Merges stdout and stderr.

tools.name: read_command
tools.description: Inspect retained output. Use run_command to start processes and read_file for files. Page a command stream by id and stream from byte offset=0, then follow next_offset. For a tool result omitted from context, pass its output unchanged with offset and limit. Add stream only for a retained command stream. Streams last while their Node owner retains them. Canonical tool results survive restart. A waited read reports data.wait as matched, output, exited or deadline.

id.description: Exact UUID from run_command data.id (background), sailry_command.id (foreground) or the command list. Omit or pass null to list this session's commands.

wait_ms.description: With id, wait for new output, exit or deadline. Zero or omitted reads immediately.

until.description: Requires id and positive wait_ms. Match a new occurrence of this substring in either stream after this read begins. Exit or deadline also returns.

tools.name: stop_command
tools.description: Stop a background command and its process group in this session. Pass the exact UUID returned as data.id by run_command or a listed command id; never a PID, filename or command text.

id.description: Exact background command UUID from run_command data.id or a listed command id

tools.name: write_command
tools.description: Send input to a running background command in this session. Pass the exact UUID returned as data.id by run_command or a listed command id (never a PID, filename or command text) and the input exactly, including a newline when submitting a line. Accepts at most 64 KiB of UTF-8 input. A success acknowledges queued input; use read_command to inspect the response. Cannot write to another session or a finished command. Writing to a command running with workspace access needs no approval; otherwise it follows the current permission policy.

id.description: Exact background command UUID from run_command data.id or a listed command id

input.description: Input queued atomically; at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes per write

encoding.label: Some output could not be decoded
